answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% cut to component spend, and the incumbent contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. The line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so minimizing delivery risk rules out switching primary vendor or adding a second source mid-cycle (incumbent integration stability, per c1, is what is keeping deliveries on schedule). C6 shows the incumbent has previously unlocked real unit-cost reductions through multi-year commitments, and c4 shows benchmarking against market rates moved them on price AND payment terms — directly relevant to hitting an 18% cost cut without expanding scope. C2 confirms the low-cost alternate vendor's invoicing accuracy, useful as leverage/benchmark in negotiation but not as a switch target this cycle given the no-buffer constraint. Verifying c2 and c6 grounds both the negotiating leverage (market rate benchmark) and the incumbent's track record on structural cost concessions (volume pricing via term length) before committing. Intended action: negotiate_terms — propose a multi-year commitment to the incumbent in exchange for the 18% unit-cost reduction and improved payment terms, using the low-cost vendor's pricing as the benchmark anchor. Outcome measurement: achieved unit-cost reduction vs. 18% target, payment-term improvement, delivery continuity through the transition window. If negotiation falls short of the 18% target, escalate to switch_primary_vendor at the next review cycle once buffer stock can be built.
